columbia-hanford.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (batch 2). Both endpoints are verified. Vernita Bridge comes from WDFW's field-confirmed ramp feature 25 plus the WDFW page and the WaterAccessSites layer. White Bluffs comes from USFWS's own facility asset point plus USFWS Hanford Reach pages. Banks come from NHDPlus HR. White Bluffs is closed to motorized launching Nov 1-Jun 30; non-motorized load/unload is allowed.

cowlitz.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (batch 1). Tacoma Power confirms both launches (Barrier Dam, Blue Creek) are public and free, but it publishes addresses only. WDFW's Barrier Dam ramp feature sits at the ramp head in the lot, about 30-35 m from the water. Blue Creek has no agency ramp feature. Pending until on-ramp agency coordinates are found for both.

grande-ronde-lower.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (batch 2). Both endpoints are verified. Troy comes from OSMB (ODFW-managed) and Heller Bar from WDFW ramp feature 244 (Chief Joseph Wildlife Area Unit). Banks come from NHDPlus HR. The Heller Bar take-out is on the Snake's west bank (river-left) just below the confluence.

grande-ronde-troy.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (batch 2). Both endpoints are verified. Troy (Oregon) comes from the Oregon State Marine Board boating-access point (ODFW-managed) plus the BLM river page. Boggan's comes from WDFW ramp feature 250 plus the WDFW page and the WaterAccessSites layer. Banks come from NHDPlus HR. BLM requires free self-issued river permits for boating in Oregon.

green-flaming-geyser.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (final run). Whitney Bridge is verified (King County Parks non-motorized put-in feature 327). Flaming Geyser State Park is still pending (no State Parks launch coordinate).

green-gorge.note: Reviewed 2026-11-09: Tacoma Water confirms controlled raft/kayak access at Headworks. Headworks, Kanaskat-Palmer and Flaming Geyser retain approximate facility-area precision, restrictions and separate section reviews; no exact landing GPS is claimed.

hoh.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (final run). Both endpoints still pending: no NPS launch POI at Hoh Rain Forest; DNR confirms Oxbow's hand boat launch but its coordinate is the campground.

klickitat.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (batch 1). All three endpoints (Leidl, Mineral Springs/Icehouse, Turkey Hole) are verified. Coordinates come from WDFW's Facilities GIS ramp/hand-launch features, checked on Esri World Imagery. Access comes from WDFW water-access pages and the WaterAccessSites layer (WDFW-managed, no closure). Banks come from NHDPlus HR flowlines. Turkey Hole is take-out only and the last designated take-out above Lyle Falls.

methow-lower.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (batch 2). Carlton and Averill/McFarland are verified (WDFW ramp features 108 and 89). Pateros Take-out is still pending: its manager is unknown and there is no agency coordinate.

methow-upper.note: Audited 2026-10-25. Pending: Big Eddy (Methow), Red Barn Access (Winthrop), Twisp Access not yet confirmed at the exact river-side launch by a current managing-agency source. Maps stay hidden until every endpoint is verified.

queets.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (final run). All endpoints pending: NPS launch POIs for Hartzell and Streaters are off the water on imagery; the NPS Queets Campground launch is 427 m from Queets Trailhead (relabel decision needed).

sauk.note: Audited 2026-10-25. Pending: Government Bridge (Sauk), Lower Sauk Boat Launch, Sauk Prairie (Darrington) not yet confirmed at the exact river-side launch by a current managing-agency source. Maps stay hidden until every endpoint is verified.

skagit-eagle.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (final run). Copper Creek is verified (NPS POI 20467). Marblemount (USFS coordinate is the parking loop) and Howard Miller (Skagit County, no public coordinate) are still pending.

skagit-upper.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (final run). Both endpoints are verified from NPS Public POIs (Goodell Creek Raft Launch 33925, Copper Creek Raft Take-out/Launch 20467) plus the NPS North Cascades rafting page, checked on Esri imagery. Banks come from NHDPlus HR. No fee for personal rafts (NPS).

skykomish.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (final run). Lewis Street and Big Eddy (WDFW hand launch 27; State Parks-managed) are verified. Sultan Sportsman Park is still pending.

spokane.note: Audited 2026-10-25. Pending: Plese Flats, T.J. Meenach Bridge not yet confirmed at the exact river-side launch by a current managing-agency source. Maps stay hidden until every endpoint is verified.

wenatchee-leavenworth.note: Audited 2026-10-25 (final run). Peshastin and Dryden Dam are verified (WDFW hand-launch features 57 and 49). Waterfront Park (Leavenworth) and Cashmere Riverside Park are still pending (city sites, no public coordinates).

white-salmon.note: Audited 2026-10-25. Pending: BZ Corner, Husum (above the falls) not yet confirmed at the exact river-side launch by a current managing-agency source. Maps stay hidden until every endpoint is verified.

Big Horn Recreation Site.accessType: Launch (open gravel/sand clearing to the water)
Big Horn Recreation Site.operator: Bureau of Land Management (Wenatchee Field Office)
Big Horn Recreation Site.sourceName: Access: BLM Yakima River Canyon page (lists Bighorn among BLM's five developed river access sites). Coordinate: North's own Google Maps marking, checked on Esri World Imagery
Big Horn Recreation Site.note: IMAGERY-PLACED: coordinate placed from satellite imagery and confirmed by North's own circled marking and Google Maps coordinate (46.8939898, -120.5004652), checked on Esri World Imagery z19 (z20 not available), 2026-10-25. Agency published no exact launch coordinate: BLM's National Recreation Site Points layer has no Bighorn feature. On imagery (research/raw/batch4/bhN.png, bhN_w.png, bh19c_g.png) the point sits inside an open gravel/sand clearing that runs from a small paved pull-off and structure beside SR 821 down to the Yakima's north-east shore. The clearing's water-side tip is about 8.5 m SSW (~46.89392, -120.50051). The point is not in the water, not on the road and not in the paved lot (the lot edge is ~15 m NE). Offsets: 426 m SE of the earlier v1/AW candidate (46.8965, -120.5047, an opening near the campground's NW end, now superseded); ~130 m SE of the Google 'Bighorn Boat Ramp' label pin. Our georeference of North's screenshot (Esri features + scale bar) gave a water end within ~9 m of this point. Legal access: BLM's Yakima River Canyon page (https://www.blm.gov/visit/yakima-river-canyon-campgrounds) lists it among BLM's five developed river access sites (Bighorn, Umtanum, Lmuma Creek, Big Pines, Roza), open year-round; fees $5 day-use, $15 overnight. Spot-check first: no ramp surface is visible (natural launch), and the imagery date is unknown.
Big Horn Recreation Site.bankSourceName: USGS NHDPlus HR flowline (flow-direction digitized) + Esri World Imagery
Big Horn Recreation Site.bankNote: Facing downstream (NHDPlus HR flow bearing ~128, SE through the canyon), the launch is on the north-east bank, left of the NHD centreline (~41 m; ftype 558 artificial path). On imagery SR 821 runs along the same (left) bank and the railway along the opposite (right, south-west) bank.

Flaming Geyser State Park.note: The current State Parks page and brochure describe kayaking on the park’s Green River frontage. Carry boats using an open permitted river-access path and identify your shoreline entry or exit during the shuttle. Discover Pass required; respect gate hours and posted closures.

Headworks (Green River).directions: Check in with the Tacoma Water gate guard on SE Green River Headworks Road and obtain permission before entering. Follow the guard’s directions to the designated boating access below the diversion. Bring identification and vehicle insurance documentation; the published access agreement requires these. Launch during daylight and use only the approved access and parking. The Area marker is not an entrance gate or exact landing.
Headworks (Green River).note: Tacoma Water’s management plan (printed p. 28) explicitly identifies raft and kayak launching at the upper gravel placement site below the diversion. Its March 2007 access map, hosted by agreement participant American Whitewater, matches the road, buildings and river in current imagery. This is controlled boating access, not general public access to the watershed. The plan excludes unchaperoned swimming, picnicking and inner-tubing. Current gate instructions control; no agency GPS landing fix or verified bank is claimed.

County Topographic Atlas 2011 page 49 labels Howard Miller Boat Launch here, and the county’s September 2011 kiosk notice independently names this launch. The existing research candidate projects to UTM 10N 603813 E, 5371106 N, matching the atlas launch vicinity; imagery shows the river-side lot west of SR 530. Trees obscure the precise ramp end. Howard Miller Steelhead Park.sourceName: Skagit County Parks and Recreation — Howard Miller Steelhead Park
Howard Miller Steelhead Park.directions: Use Howard Miller Steelhead Park, 52804 Rockport Park Road, Rockport. Follow park signs to the river launch west of the SR 530 bridge. Check current launch fees and posted conditions with the county; the Area marker does not identify the exact waterline.

Husum (above the falls).note: Current USFS page identifies this boating/portage facility and publishes the unchanged candidate coordinate. Individual imagery places it at the roadside pull-out upstream of the visible falls. Preserve Area precision: the water-entry path and take-out eddy are under tree cover. Missing the upstream exit can lead into Class V Husum Falls.

Husum (above the falls).sourceName: USDA Forest Service — Husum (above the falls)
